newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London edge higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London edge higher in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. stocks trading in London were slightly higher in sympathy with a firm performance in New York overnight, but trade remained thin ahead of the Christmas holidays, dealers said.
"We're fractionally higher but there are no major features it's very quiet trade," said one trader.

The Dow staged its first significant rally in a week on Tuesday to close almost 40 points better at 6,308.33, partly on relief that the FOMC left interest rates unchanged. "There was an outside chance that the Fed could have raised interest rates, but now that fear has gone," a trader said.
In the absence of any major scheduled corporate or economic news in the U.S. today, traders expect activity to remain sudued.
"We will maybe be up 10-12 points at the opening," one said. "But I don't think the market will do much either way, it has got that Chistmassy feel.

Among individual share movers General Electric was marked $1/2 higher to $98-1/4 in anticipation of Friday's board meeting. Analysts expect General Electric to raise the dividend payout by around 13 percent, split the company's stock two-for-one and also consider additional stock repurchases.
Elsewhere, oil drillers benefited from press reports that George Soros liked the sector and was increasing his holdings in oil services.
Schlumberger was up $3/8 at $100-1/4. Halliburton put on $1/4 at $57-3/4 and Baker Hughes was $1/4 better at $35-1/4.
